newsitem.title: ITALY: Omnitel has 560,000 GSM users at end-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Omnitel has 560,000 GSM users at end-Sept.

text.p: Italy's second mobile phone operator Omnitel said it had 560,000 subscribers for its GSM digital mobile phone network by the end of September.
Omnitel managing director Silvio Scaglia told a news conference the company's rate of subscriber growth was the fastest in the world in the sector.

The short-term aim of Omnitel, in which Olivetti has a 41.3 percent stake, was to have 700,000 clients by the end of 1996. "It is worth recalling that at the start of this year forecasts talked of 400,000 subscribers," Scaglia said.
At end-September, Omnitel's network covered 55 percent of the country, serving 82 percent of the population, he added.
He said the subscriber cancellation or churn rate was 1.1 percent per month, equal to an annual rate of 12-13 percent.
Press reports have speculated on a much higher rate.
"This is all rubbish. Our churn rate is well below global levels which reach three percent a month," Scaglia said.
Omnitel launched its mobile GSM service in December 1995, and had gained 500,000 subscribers by the end of August.
Italy's largest mobile phone group, state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM), started its GSM service in early 1995 and its latest official figures put its GSM users at 971,501 at September 18.
Total TIM mobile phone users were 4.78 million at the same date when taking into account its older analogue mobile phone network as well as GSM users.
Scaglia confirmed Omnitel's objective of breaking even in 1998. The group reported a net loss of 260 billion lire in the first half of 1996.
Replying to questions, he said he was unable to put a precise value on the company.

"I've heard estimates of a minimum six trillion lire and a top figure of 12 trillion, but it's not up to us to calculate Omnitel's current value, it's up to the market. But whatever it is we want to double it in four years," he said.
Referring to problems at troubled Olivetti, Scaglia underlined that Omnitel was a completely separate entity.

"For Olivetti were are its best investment and certainly for us Olivetti is very important. We are very worried over what's happening there. But we are completely separated from Olivetti from a financial point of view," he said.

Over the likelihood of a stock market listing for Omnitel, Scaglia said that for now "the possibility of a bourse quotation has not been examined." Omnitel's wholly paid-up equity currently totalled 1.45 trillion lire, he said.
Omnitel had 2,400 employees and was looking to take on another 150 in coming months, he added. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
